newsitem.title: USA: U.S. money managers extend US debt positions--MCM.
newsitem.headline: U.S. money managers extend US debt positions--MCM.

text.p: U.S. fixed-income managers modestly extended the durations of their U.S. debt portfolios in the past week, according to an MCM MoneyWatch Inc survey.
The weekly survey showed durations as a percentage of benchmark rose to 106.8 percent from 106.5, in the week ended February 3.
"(It) would appear there's more interest at these levels given the uptick in buys," said MCM money market analyst Peter McTeague, who conducts the asset allocation survey.
"Maybe (debt portfolio managers) think the worst is priced in for now," he said.
A duration reading above 100 percent indicates the group of investors polled is mostly long on the market.
A portfolio's duration represents its average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
In the "next likely move" category, portfolio managers representing 38 percent of total assets in the survey said they would "buy," compared with 29 percent the prior week.
Strategists leaning toward "sell" dropped to 11 percent, down from 22 percent in the week ended January 27.
Fifty-one percent of managers said they were "neutral" on the market, up from 49 percent a week ago.
Cash as a percentage of assets rose to 3.10 percent, against 3.0 percent registered the previous week.

The survey showed 29 percent of investors polled overweighted the 10-plus years duration sector, up from 25 percent the previous week, while 12 percent underweighted it. The remaining 59 percent were "neutral."
In the five- to 10-year duration sector, 41 percent of investors polled said they overweighted the securities and 12 percent underweighted them.
The survey included 38 domestic participants, who manage about $110 billion in fixed-income assets. The poll is conducted weekly by MCM and usually is released on Tuesday.
